title: A helicopter made 72 flights on Mars
body: On 19 April 2021, NASA's Ingenuity became the first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another world. It went on to fly 72 times before its mission ended.
takeaway: An aerial scout can examine terrain beyond the view from a rover's cameras close to the ground.
visual: a small helicopter airborne above a rocky Martian plain

title: Astronauts corrected Hubble's vision without replacing its mirror
body: After Hubble's 1990 launch, NASA found a flaw in the primary mirror that blurred images. In December 1993, astronauts installed instruments with optics that compensated for how the mirror bent the light.
takeaway: A known error in one part can sometimes be counteracted elsewhere in the optical path.
visual: an astronaut working beside the open instrument bay of a space telescope

title: Webb's primary mirror was folded for launch
body: The James Webb Space Telescope's main mirror uses 18 hexagonal segments that together span about 6.5 metres. Hinged sections folded to fit into the launch rocket and opened after separation.
takeaway: A folding design lets a telescope use a wider mirror than its rocket can carry in one flat piece.
source: NASA Science, Webb's Mirrors and FAQs
visual: gold mirror segments opening on the wing of a space telescope
